# A vessel over a popup that covers the main window re-enters main first

## Context

Operator hand test, 2026-09-26 ~09:20Z, on dev with #19242 and #19244 merged and themes rebuilt: a tab torn out and dragged over another popup still does not convert into the inline proxy, no drop zones show, a tab cannot be dropped into a popup this way. Every automated witness (the region probe, the film driver, `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL`) places the target popup OUTSIDE the main window; on one screen a popup normally lies OVER the main window's dock root.

**Reproduced with that placement** (headed, real `page.mouse` drag, CDP focus emulation off; main 1320×920 pinned, target popup 700×500 placed over main's content at +300/+200, the held pointer walked from outside main onto the popup's content at fx 0.15 / fy 0.3; receipts `test-results/dock-wow-demo/hand-conversion/2026-09-26/2026-09-26T09-34-36-647Z-hand-real-focus.json`): during the walk the vessel window CLOSED (`vessel page closed=true`) before the popup could claim — the source-root re-entry fired and the vessel morphed back into main; the gesture then continued as an in-window tab drag over a popup lying on main, produced one stray `converted: true` frame with the native-path receipt "main-window target: nothing to park, the popup retires after the commit", and the TARGET popup closed. The same walk with the target beside main (two runs, focus emulation off and on) converts and parks cleanly. So the failure is not focus, not the admission metric, not the still pointer: it is the re-entry rule.

## Measurement update (2026-09-26 09:50Z) — the premise above is NOT reproduced

Two more headed runs, target placed over main BEFORE the tear-out and the held pointer entering through the popup's title-bar strip (receipts `strip-dev/` and `strip-fix/` under the same folder): on dev the vessel did **not** morph on the strip — a 480×360 vessel covers too little of main's root for the coverage test (0.18 < 0.6) — and the same on the fix. The first overlap run's "vessel closed" was the designed return over 300 px of EXPOSED main that the walk crossed, and the target popup closing in every over-main run was an instrument artifact: placing a committed popup over main by CDP drives the native title-bar path, whose dwell commits the popup into main. So this ticket's mechanism is a derivation, not a measurement. The fix and its red-first arm stay on a local branch; no PR until the operator's own gesture receipts (park receipt, claim ring) say which admission refuses. Status: premise unverified.

## The Problem

`Neo.draggable.container.SortZone#checkWindowBoundary` (window-drag branch) fires `dragBoundaryEntry` — the morph back into the source — when the vessel-sized proxy's coverage of the source root rises above `reattachThreshold` while armed. It reads only the source root's rect. `Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.TabSortZone#checkWindowBoundary` suppresses that only while `pointerClaimArbiter.resolve()` returns a live claim, and a claim needs the pointer inside the target's INNER rect plus `acceptsRemoteDrag`. A popup covering the source root therefore has a strip — its title bar (67 px on macOS Chrome) and any exposed source root the path crosses — where the pointer is over the popup's frame, no claim exists yet, and the proxy already covers enough of the source root: the re-entry wins and the vessel retires. The hand always crosses that strip; the drivers never did.

## Design authority

ADR 0029 §2.8.1: *"Hit-claims on stable identity … no claim — fail closed: no preview, no commit"* — a claim decides target ownership; nothing in the record makes the source root's rect an authority over frames a target window covers. §2.8.2's machine: `DETACHED_MOVING → HOVERING_CLAIM`; the re-entry (`TabSortZone` JSDoc: "the real return-to-source transition") is the source's own outcome and must not fire on a frame the pointer spends over another window. The operator's expected behavior (this morning): the vessel over another popup converts to the tab-header proxy and shows the target's drop zones. Decision Record impact: `aligned-with ADR 0029` (no sentence changes).

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs` `checkWindowBoundary` (~:330-445): the coverage sampler and the armed re-entry.
- `src/dashboard/dock/interaction/TabSortZone.mjs` `checkWindowBoundary` (~:362): the claim-only suppression.
- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs`: `sortZones` (Map: sortGroup → Map: windowId → zone) is the registry of every window that can be a target; `getWindowAtExcept(x, y, excluded)` already tests `Window.items[].outerRect` against a point.
- `src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs` (~:576, :640): the window-drag move payload carries `screenX` / `screenY`.
- `src/manager/Window.mjs`: `outerRect` is the frame incl. chrome; the vessel window itself has no registered zone in the sort group.

## The Fix

`TabSortZone#checkWindowBoundary`: while `isWindowDragging`, treat a frame as remote territory not only when a claim resolves but also when the pointer (`data.screenX` / `screenY`) lies inside the OUTER rect of any window registered in the zone's sort group other than the source window (the vessel has no registered zone, so it never matches itself) — return `true` without consulting the base sampler. The popup's content then claims on the next frame the pointer reaches it; its title-bar strip becomes a hold; leaving the popup onto exposed source root still re-enters (the designed return).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC-1 (unit, red-first): `DockTabSortZone.spec.mjs` › `checkWindowBoundary`: with no claim, a pointer inside a registered sibling window's outer rect suppresses the base sampler (no `dragBoundaryEntry`, no `onWindowDragContinue`); with the pointer outside every registered window the base sampler runs as before; the source window's own rect never suppresses.
- AC-2 (headed, one run, real windows): the hand-conversion probe in overlap placement at the fix head — the vessel stays open through the walk, the popup claims, `converted: true`, `parked: true`, the preview renders inside the popup; both beside-main runs unchanged.
- AC-3 (CI): `unit/dashboard` green.

## Out of Scope

- The claim tie when the source is itself a popup and the target popup lies over main: both main and the target claim, and §2.8.1's lexicographic tiebreak lets `workstation-main` win over any `workstation-vessel:*` id although the popup is the visible window. Derived, not measured; noted for the record's author as a §2.8.1 amendment candidate (a nested candidate outranks the enclosing one).
- The embodiment shape (the target-side proxy must be the tab header, not the window content): the operator's design call, filed separately.
